checks.accrual: Defaults are 600 eligible original value failures, 2,048 collection-source cap, initial 512 then complete 256-source chunks. Only usable valid-schema originals with at least one wrong typed value count. Selection freezes after accrual, uses the saved ranking_seed=255777 permutation, takes the first 600 eligible IDs (or all available at cap), with no severity ranking.
checks.audit: 96 separately seeded audit sources use the selected tier and separate audit split/index range. Their calls occur after the collection selection is frozen. Audit outcomes are reported separately and cannot accrue or enter either paired arm.
checks.stopping: Accrual checks only the original collection failure count at complete chunk boundaries. Intervention outcomes are unavailable to the collector. The paired phase computes recovery only after all scheduled jobs settle; infrastructure failures stop dispatch without orchestration retries.
checks.paired_design: Each selected original receives one fresh generate request and one feedback-repair request, both with the same source input hash. Default max_workers=4 runs randomized four-request blocks containing both arms for two cases; no request receives another arm's answer.
checks.request_content: Solver inputs are restricted to case_id, task_instructions and documents. Fresh requests have null feedback. Repair requests contain the model's original response and only generic wrong-field/schema/evidence flags; the builder does not pass gold, expected values, or calculation traces.
checks.identity_and_cache: The full canonical request determines the SHA256 cache key. Cache files are deterministic gzip JSON written atomically and retain the full request, raw stdout/stderr, events, parsed response, usage and diagnostics. Case content_hash and request_input_hash are carried through the plan, candidate, ledger and paired-source equality checks.
checks.transport: One Codex CLI subprocess per request, high reasoning effort, 900-second hashed timeout, empty temporary working directory, user config/rules ignored, read-only sandbox and tool/plugin features disabled. The runner records reconnect/error events and does not claim to disable internal CLI network retry behavior.
checks.namespace_and_replay: The authoring collector executes helper source in an explicit namespace and verifies frozen source hashes. The fixture wrapper executes the three frozen source cores in isolated namespaces and checks byte hashes. The phase CLI is offline unless --live is supplied; phases are separate and are not automatically chained.
checks.source_gate: The fixture writer audits rendered sources before freezing compressed JSONL; independent SQL/Decimal and text/Fraction checks are invoked. Existing source packs are checked against the declared generation size, seed, tier, split and index range before use. Prior source inventory excludes temporary/checkpoint paths and response exports, and checks source IDs and normalized semantic hashes.
checks.diagnostics: Metrics separate value, evidence-only, schema, unusable and transport outcomes; audit metrics remain separate. The primary decision is positive repair-minus-fresh value recovery plus two-sided exact McNemar p<0.05. Bootstrap intervals use paired cases; reconnect sensitivity is reported separately. USD spend is null/unknown rather than zero.

nonblocking_observations: Configuration permits max_workers=1 or 2 as well as 4. At a value below 4, scale_dispatch_waves splits the prepared four-job blocks into smaller actual dispatch waves, so wording that says each runtime wave contains four requests is no longer literal. The default is 4, and lower concurrency does not expose outcomes or change the fixed paired estimand; if used, report the actual max_workers and wave size from the frozen protocol.
